question: What is the scientific classification of the starless object “Cloud-9” discovered by NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope in January 2026?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Reionization-Limited H I Cloud.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__** 

__
 
• **NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope identified Cloud-9 as a Reionization-Limited H I Cloud, a starless dark-matter-dominated relic from the early universe.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Cloud-9 is classified as a Reionization-Limited H I Cloud or RELHIC.**
 
• It is composed mainly of neutral hydrogen and contains no stars.
 
• The object is dominated by dark matter and is considered a failed or relic galaxy.
 
• Cloud-9__ 
 __
 
• Located about 14 million light-years from Earth near galaxy M94
 
• Detected by FAST, VLA and confirmed by Hubble
 
• Provides insight into early galaxy formation
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

__
 
• RELHIC__

 __
 
• A theoretical type of primordial hydrogen cloud that failed to form stars after cosmic reionization.
 
 
 
• Neutral Hydrogen H I__
 __
 
• Hydrogen atoms that have not lost their electrons, commonly found in interstellar gas clouds.
 
 
 
• Dark Matter__
 __
 
• Invisible matter that makes up most of the universe’s mass and governs galaxy formation through gravity.
 
 
 
• Hubble Space Telescope__
 
 
• A joint NASA and ESA observatory used to study distant galaxies, stars and cosmic phenomena.
